articles.title_original: Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
articles.title_zh: Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
facts_zh:
Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says
- Published
At least 26 people were killed after Russian bombs hit an aid distribution centre, in an attack that Ukraine's leader has called "utterly horrific".

Five people were injured and 27 initially reported missing after at least nine 3,000kg aerial bombs hit the village of Komyshuvakha in the southern Zaporizhzhia region, regional head Mykhailo Semikin said.
President Volodymyr Zelensky said that after the first strike on the local school "used for humanitarian needs", there was a second attack on the place where people were sheltering.

all_titles.en: Russian bombing kills 26 people at Ukraine aid centre, Kyiv says

articles.title_original: Man guilty of stealing cash from farm owned by South African president
articles.title_zh: Man guilty of stealing cash from farm owned by South African president
facts_zh:
Man guilty of stealing cash from farm owned by South African president
- Published
A court in South Africa has found a man guilty of stealing more than $500,000 (£372,822) in cash from a farm owned by South African president Cyril Ramaphosa, in a case that mired the head of state in an impeachment saga.
Imanuwela David was found guilty of theft on Monday, as well as conspiracy to commit housebreaking with intent to steal at Phala Phala farm in the Limpopo province in 2020.
Froliana Joseph, a cleaner at the property, was also found guilty of conspiracy to commit housebreaking with intent to steal.

all_titles.en: Man guilty of stealing cash from farm owned by South African president

articles.title_original: Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal
articles.title_zh: Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal
facts_zh:
Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal
- Published
US President Donald Trump has notified Congress of his intention to remove South Africa and Rwanda from a preferential trade programme, from 1 January 2027.
The African Growth and Opportunity Act (Agoa) allows eligible African countries to export thousands of products to the US duty-free.
US Trade Representative Jamieson Greer said in a statement that an annual review had found that both countries were engaging in practices inconsistent with the programme's eligibility requirements.

all_titles.en: Trump to remove Rwanda and South Africa from US trade deal

articles.title_original: Fake nuclear warning from hacked app sparks unease but not panic in Ukraine
articles.title_zh: Fake nuclear warning from hacked app sparks unease but not panic in Ukraine
facts_zh:
Fake nuclear warning from hacked app sparks unease but not panic in Ukraine
- Published
Ukrainians have grown weary of the relentless alerts blaring from their phones and echoing through their streets, day and night, warning of Russian drones and missiles.

On Sunday night, the system delivered something to make them sit up and take note – a succession of more extreme threats that quickly escalated to impending nuclear strikes, chemical attacks and combat on the streets.
But many in the country did not take them seriously and doubted the veracity of the messages.

all_titles.en: Fake nuclear warning from hacked app sparks unease but not panic in Ukraine

articles.title_original: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
articles.title_zh: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
facts_zh:
Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack
- Published
Dozens of supermarkets across seven European countries have been hit by a cyber-attack affecting their refrigerators and freezers.
Around 40 Delhaize supermarkets in Belgium and Luxembourg were affected, while a smaller number of shops were hit in Sweden, Ireland, the Netherlands, Estonia and Finland.

Sabcobel, a Belgian company that manufactures some of the affected refrigerators, said the units' evaporators were switched to defrost mode, causing them to warm up, in what is believed to be the same method used in last month's incident that hit hundreds of French supermarkets.

all_titles.en: Shop freezers in seven European countries hit by cyber-attack

articles.title_original: Fighting returns to Kherson region after longest Ukraine war ceasefire
articles.title_zh: Fighting returns to Kherson region after longest Ukraine war ceasefire
facts_zh:
Fighting returns to Kherson region after longest Ukraine war ceasefire
- Published
Fighting has resumed in Ukraine's Kherson after a six-day truce brought quiet to the front-line region for the first time in years.

The ceasefire - the longest since the start of Russia's full-scale invasion in 2022 - allowed hundreds of people trapped in the Russian-occupied Ukrainian town of Oleshky and its surroundings to be evacuated.
On Monday morning, local authorities confirmed that strikes had resumed, saying Moscow had hit a medical facility in Kherson city centre.

all_titles.en: Fighting returns to Kherson region after longest Ukraine war ceasefire

articles.title_original: Dutch police offer record €2m reward in hunt for drug lord
articles.title_zh: Dutch police offer record €2m reward in hunt for drug lord
facts_zh:
Dutch police offer record €2m reward in hunt for drug lord
- Published
Dutch authorities have offered a record award of €2m (£1.7m/$2.24m) for information leading to the arrest of Jos Leijdekkers, one of Europe's most-wanted men.
The 35-year-old, who is also known as Bolle Jos (Chubby Jos), was previously accused of being "one of the key players in international cocaine trafficking" by Dutch police.

Commenting on the decision to increase the reward ten-fold, Dutch justice minister David van Weel said it was "necessary given the threat that Leijdekkers poses to national security, our democratic rule of law, and the international legal order".

all_titles.en: Dutch police offer record €2m reward in hunt for drug lord

facts_zh:
Wizz Air flight from Luton in emergency landing after bomb threat
- Published
A Wizz Air flight travelling from London Luton Airport to Sofia has been escorted by a Hungarian fighter jet to Budapest after a mid-air bomb threat.
The aircraft was forced to make an emergency landing at Budapest Liszt Ferenc International.
Authorities there "carried out the necessary security checks on the aircraft and passengers", a spokesperson for Wizz Air said.

articles.title_original: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
articles.title_zh: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
facts_zh:
Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares
- Published
Ryanair is considering a temporary wage freeze for staff and confirmed airfares will be "materially higher" next summer because of a sharp rise in fuel costs following the US-Israel war with Iran.
The airline said it expects fuel prices to remain high "well into 2027" unless there is a "swift resolution" to the conflict.
Ryanair said its fuel bill is forecast to be €2bn (£1.6bn) higher in the short-term and its boss, Michael O'Leary, said airfares would have to rise by "double-digits" to help cover the cost.

all_titles.en: Ryanair says it may freeze workers' pay and raise airfares

articles.title_original: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
articles.title_zh: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
facts_zh:
Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years
- Published
Uganda has begun withdrawing its troops from Somalia after nearly two decades of military involvement in the country.

Uganda's acting army spokesperson Chris Magezi on Monday said the first group of troops deployed to Somalia through a bilateral arrangement had already arrived back home and others would follow in a few days' time.
He said all forces, including those under the African Union (AU) mission, would exit by the end of 2027 in the phased withdrawal.

all_titles.en: Uganda begins withdrawing troops from Somalia after 20 years

articles.title_zh: Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured
facts_zh:
Five arrested after South African farmer shot and tortured
- Published
Warning: This article contains graphic details that some people may find distressing
South African police have arrested five people in connection with a brutal attack on a cattle farmer, who was assaulted and tortured in what has been described as a "senseless and barbaric" act.
Donovan Marx, 50, was attacked during a house robbery on his farm in Ventersdorp, a small town in South Africa's North West province, last Wednesday.
Marx was ambushed as he returned home, shot and stabbed and had his ears cut off in the horrific ordeal, police said.
